Optimal.Notes: Native 1280x800 at high textures with a 40 fps/40 Hz lock delivers a sharp, fluid experience that matches the game's artistic intent. This is the recommended daily-driver profile.

profiles.Summary: Disco Elysium – The Final Cut is a narrative RPG with a painterly isometric art style and very modest GPU demands, well within the Steam Deck's capabilities even at native resolution. It runs smoothly on Deck with no special tuning required, and the hardware can comfortably push 60 fps while sipping battery.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the very modest PC minimum/recommended requirements and the Deck's hardware capabilities. On your first run, check the frame counter in a busy outdoor area (e.g. the Whirling-in-Rags courtyard) and drop to the Optimal profile if you see unexpected dips.

MaxBattery.Notes: At 5 W TDP and a 30 fps cap the Deck barely breaks a sweat with this lightweight engine; battery life is excellent. The 40 Hz refresh rate keeps motion smooth at the 30 fps cap.

KnownIssues: Some players report small on-screen text that can be hard to read on the 7-inch display; increasing UI scale in accessibility settings helps.
Occasional audio desync or crackling has been noted under Proton; switching to Proton Experimental can resolve it.
The game may default to a windowed or borderless mode on first launch; manually setting fullscreen in options is recommended.

MaxPerformance.Notes: The game's engine is light enough that max settings at 60 fps is realistic on the Deck; GPU and CPU headroom remains large throughout. TDP is capped at 12 W to avoid unnecessary heat while still allowing burst headroom.
